Moment of inertia of solid cylinder of mass M and radius R about its axis:

In YDSE, fringe width is β. If the entire setup is immersed in water (n = 4/3), the new fringe width is:
β = λD/d. In water, λ' = λ/n. So β' = β/n = β × 3/4. Wavelength reduces in denser medium.
A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 30 m/s in 10 s. The distance covered in this time is:
A wave is described by y = 0.05 sin(50πt − 0.5πx) where x, y in meters and t in seconds. The wavelength is:
Compare with y = A sin(ωt − kx). k = 0.5π. Wavelength λ = 2π/k = 2π/(0.5π) = 4 m. Also, ω = 50π → f = 25 Hz; wave speed v = ω/k = 50π/(0.5π) = 100 m/s.
The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through 150 V is approximately:
λ = 12.27/√V Å (for non-relativistic electrons). At V = 150: λ = 12.27/√150 ≈ 12.27/12.25 ≈ 1.00 Å. More precisely: λ = h/√(2meV) gives same result.
The orbital velocity at Earth's surface (g=9.8, R=6.4×10⁶ m):
v = √(gR) = √(9.8 × 6.4×10⁶) = √(6.27×10⁷) = 7920 m/s = 7.9 km/s. First cosmic velocity.
Mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. For convex mirror with f = +20 cm, u = −30 cm, v is:
Two equal positive charges are placed on x-axis at x = +a and x = −a. The electric field at origin (0,0) is:
Field from each charge at origin has magnitude kq/a². They point in opposite directions, so they cancel. Net E = 0 at origin. However, potential at origin is 2kq/a (non-zero).
The wavelength of the first line of Lyman series of hydrogen atom is (R = 1.097×10⁷ m⁻¹):
EM waves are transverse: E and B fields oscillate perpendicular to each other and to direction of propagation.
Width of central maximum in single slit diffraction (sl width a = 0.1 mm, λ = 500 nm, screen 1 m away):
Width = 2λD/a = 2 × 500×10⁻⁹ × 1/(10⁻⁴) = 10⁻² m = 1 cm. Linear width on screen.
A body is thrown vertically upward with velocity 20 m/s from ground. Taking g = 10 m/s², the time after which its velocity becomes half of initial (in magnitude) but opposite in direction is:

Initial velocity u = 20 m/s upward. Final velocity v = −10 m/s (half magnitude, opposite direction). Using v = u − gt: −10 = 20 − 10t → 10t = 30 → t = 3 s. At t = 3 s, the body has already passed the highest point (at t = 2 s) and is descending with v = −10 m/s.
Wavelength of photon emitted in transition n=3 to n=2 of H (Balmer, red):
Two capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is:
Series: 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ = 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6. C = 6/5 = 1.2 μF. Charge on each is same; voltage divides inversely with C.
An AC circuit has X_L = 30 Ω and X_C = 10 Ω in series with R = 40 Ω. Impedance:
An inductor of 5 H carries current changing at 2 A/s. The EMF induced across inductor is:
EMF = −L × dI/dt = −5 × 2 = −10 V. Magnitude 10 V. The negative sign indicates opposition to change (Lenz's law).
Wavelength of 1 MeV gamma ray photon:
λ = hc/E = 1240×10⁻⁹ eV·m / 10⁶ eV = 1.24×10⁻¹² m = 1.24 pm. Nuclear gamma rays are very short wavelength.
For weak acid HA with Ka = 10⁻⁵ and concentration 0.1 M, the degree of dissociation α is approximately:
For weak acid: α = √(Ka/C) = √(10⁻⁵/0.1) = √(10⁻⁴) = 10⁻². So α ≈ 0.01 (1% dissociated).
6 NH₃ ligands (hexaammine), Co oxidation state = +3 (since 3 Cl⁻ outside), so cobalt(III). Counter ion is chloride (3 Cl⁻).
The DNA base pairing rule is:
Chargaff's rule: A pairs with T (2 H-bonds), G pairs with C (3 H-bonds). Complementary strands run antiparallel.
Element with highest electron affinity in halogen group:
Chlorine has highest EA in halogens (-349 kJ/mol) due to optimal balance of nuclear charge and atomic size. F has lower EA due to small size causing e-e repulsion.
Formic acid (HCOOH) reduces Tollens' reagent because:
HCOOH has -CHO-like structure (H-C=O). Reduces Tollens' (silver mirror) unlike other acids. HCOOH + [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ → CO₂ + Ag + NH₃.
The most common oxidation state of Cu:
Cu²⁺ (d⁹) is most stable in aqueous solution. Cu⁺ (d¹⁰) is stable in solid compounds but disproportionates in water.
Polythene is formed by which type of polymerization:
n CH₂=CH₂ → (−CH₂−CH₂−)ₙ. Addition polymerization (no byproduct). Common plastic; HDPE and LDPE based on branching.
H₂S gas turns lead acetate paper:
H₂S + Pb(CH₃COO)₂ → PbS (black) + 2 CH₃COOH. PbS is one of least soluble salts; characteristic test for S²⁻.
Solubility product Ksp of CaF₂ is 3.9×10⁻¹¹. Solubility s:
The reagent used to detect chloride ion is:
Cl⁻ + AgNO₃ → AgCl↓ (white) + NO₃⁻. White precipitate soluble in NH₄OH. HNO₃ ensures other anions like carbonate don't interfere.
Methyl isocyanate (CH₃NCO) leak from Union Carbide plant killed thousands. Highly toxic, attacks respiratory system.
How many moles of MgSO₄·7H₂O are there in 246 g of the compound (Mg=24, S=32, O=16, H=1)?
Molar mass = 24 + 32 + 4×16 + 7×18 = 24+32+64+126 = 246 g/mol. Moles = 246/246 = 1 mol. Each formula unit contains 7 water molecules.
3° most stable due to hyperconjugation and inductive effects of alkyl groups. Stability drives radical reactions.
Colloidal particles show random zigzag motion due to bombardment by solvent molecules. Evidence for kinetic theory.
Glucose is reducing sugar: reduces Cu²⁺ (blue) to Cu₂O (red-brown ppt). Aldehyde group oxidized to carboxylate.
Markovnikov's rule: addition of HBr to propene (CH₃-CH=CH₂) gives:
HBr adds such that H goes to C with more H's (terminal C) and Br to C with fewer H's. CH₃-CHBr-CH₃ (2-bromopropane). Forms more stable 2° carbocation intermediate.
Most common oxidation state of lanthanides:
+3 is most stable for all lanthanides. Exceptions: Eu²⁺, Yb²⁺ (4f⁷, 4f¹⁴ stable), Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰ stable).
In the extraction of iron from haematite, the reducing agent is:
In blast furnace: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. CO is actual reducing agent; CO produced by 2C + O₂ → 2CO and CO₂ + C → 2CO in lower zones.
In Bayer's process, bauxite is purified using:
Bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O) + NaOH → soluble NaAlO₂. Impurities (Fe₂O₃, SiO₂) removed. Then precipitated and calcined.
Vapor pressure lowering for 0.1 molal sucrose solution at 100°C (Kb irrelevant):
Raoult's law: P = X·P°. Solvent mole fraction decreases slightly. ΔP = X_solute × P°. For dilute solution, small decrease.
Ligands alphabetical: ammine before chlorido. Cr oxidation state: x + 4(0) + 2(−1) = +1 → x = +3. So chromium(III).
Boiling point of 1 molal KCl solution (Kb = 0.52, van't Hoff i = 2):
ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 2 × 0.52 × 1 = 1.04°C. BP = 100 + 1.04 = 101.04°C. KCl dissociates into 2 ions.
Which has highest melting point among alkali metals?
Melting point decreases down group 1 (weaker metallic bond due to larger atom). Li: 180°C, Na: 98°C, K: 64°C, Cs: 28°C.
The standard molar entropy of which substance is highest among the following?
Entropy order: gases > liquids > solids. O₂(g) has highest S. Diamond is the most ordered (lowest entropy) due to covalent network structure.
The product of reaction of acetic acid with ethanol in presence of conc. H₂SO₄ is:
Fischer esterification: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (conc. H₂SO₄ catalyst, reversible). Ester formation.
Henry's law constant for gas in liquid at 298 K relates:
Henry: p = K_H × x. Solubility (x) proportional to partial pressure (p). Used in carbonated drinks, deep-sea diving.
20 g of NaOH (M=40) is dissolved in water to make 500 mL. Molarity:
Lucas test: 3° immediate cloudiness (SN1 fastest), 2° in 5-10 min, 1° requires heating. Based on carbocation stability.
Stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl. Due to +I effect and hyperconjugation from alkyl groups stabilizing positive charge.
Number of atoms in 4 g of He (He=4, N_A = 6.022×10²³):
Aniline on diazotization with NaNO₂/HCl at 0-5°C gives:
C₆H₅NH₂ + NaNO₂ + HCl → [C₆H₅N≡N]⁺Cl⁻ (diazonium salt) at 0-5°C. Used in azo dye synthesis. Unstable above 5°C (decomposes to phenol).
Sodium thiosulphate (Na₂S₂O₃) is used in photography for:
Na₂S₂O₃ dissolves unexposed AgBr by forming soluble complex [Ag(S₂O₃)₂]³⁻. Known as 'hypo' or fixer.
Lewis structure of CO₂ shows how many lone pairs on each O:
CO₂: O=C=O. Each O has 2 lone pairs (4 electrons). Carbon has 0 lone pairs. Linear molecule, sp hybridization.
The maximum number of electrons in a subshell with l = 2 is:
Max electrons = 2(2l+1). For l=2 (d-subshell): 2(5) = 10 electrons. Subshells: s=2, p=6, d=10, f=14.
EMF of Daniel cell with [Zn²⁺] = 0.1 M and [Cu²⁺] = 1 M at 298 K (E° = 1.1 V) is:
CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O (gypsum). Sets hard. Used in casts, molds, sculptures.
Nitrogen is inert at room temperature because of:
N≡N triple bond is very strong (945 kJ/mol). High activation energy for reaction. Ammonia synthesis requires catalyst + high T.
Magnetic moment of [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ (2 unpaired electrons, octahedral):
Ni²⁺ (d⁸) in weak field (H₂O) octahedral: 2 unpaired (high spin isomer since d⁸ has 2 unpaired regardless). μ = √(2×4) = √8 = 2.83 BM.
Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. For Δn = 1: Kp = Kc·RT. N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂ has Δn = 1.
The shape of SF₄ molecule is:
SF₄ has 4 bond pairs + 1 lone pair on S (sp³d hybridization). Electronic geometry TBP, molecular shape see-saw (lone pair occupies equatorial position).
Reagent to convert ethanol to ethene:
Ethanol + conc. H₂SO₄ at 170°C → ethene + H₂O. Dehydration (elimination). At 140°C: diethyl ether (substitution).
Number of electrons, protons, neutrons in ²³Na⁺:
Number of bonds in N₂ molecule:
N≡N: 1 σ bond (from sp hybridization overlap) + 2 π bonds (from p orbital overlap). Triple bond, very strong.
For the reaction 2A → B, rate = k[A]². If concentration of A is tripled, the rate becomes:
Rate = k[A]². New rate = k(3A)² = 9k[A]² = 9 × original rate. Second order dependence.
Element with highest electron gain enthalpy (positive value):
Cl has highest electron affinity (most exothermic, −349 kJ/mol). F lower due to small size, e-e repulsion. Negative value = releases energy.
Number of pyrimidine bases in DNA:
DNA bases: purines (Adenine, Guanine) and pyrimidines (Cytosine, Thymine). RNA has Uracil instead of Thymine.
Stratosphere (15-50 km altitude) contains ozone layer, which absorbs harmful UV radiation from sun.
The standard EMF of cell with Zn|Zn²⁺ (E°=−0.76) || Ag⁺|Ag (E°=+0.80) is:
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 − (−0.76) = 1.56 V. Spontaneous reaction.
For the reaction H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g), ΔH = −185 kJ. The enthalpy of formation of HCl is:
ΔH = Σ ΔH_f(products) − Σ ΔH_f(reactants). For elements in standard state, ΔH_f = 0. So ΔH = 2 × ΔH_f(HCl). ΔH_f(HCl) = −185/2 = −92.5 kJ/mol.
Color of KMnO₄ in aqueous solution is:
Purple/violet color due to charge transfer (Mn⁷⁺ to O²⁻). Reduced to Mn²⁺ (colorless) by oxalic acid in acidic medium.
The most acidic compound among the following is:
Formic acid (HCOOH) is more acidic than acetic acid (CH₃COOH) because methyl group donates electron density (+I effect), destabilizing carboxylate. Order: HCOOH > CH₃COOH.
Bond energy decreases down group (larger atom = longer bond = weaker). H-F (570 kJ/mol) > H-Cl (432) > H-Br (366) > H-I (298).
Compounds with same molecular formula but different structures are called:
Isomerism: same formula, different arrangement. Allotropes (different forms of element), homologs (differ by CH₂), isotopes (same element, different neutrons).
Relation between Kp and Kc for general gas reaction:
Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn where Δn = moles gas products − moles gas reactants. Δn = 0: Kp = Kc. Δn > 0: Kp > Kc.
Standard electrode potential for Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34 V. ΔG° for Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ is (F = 96500):
ΔG° = −nFE° = −2 × 96500 × (−0.34) = +65.6 kJ/mol (for oxidation, reverse sign: +65.6 kJ). Non-spontaneous oxidation.
Boron (Group 13, Period 2) shows diagonal relationship with Mg (Group 2, Period 3). Both have similar charge/radius ratio. Be-Al and B-Si also show diagonal relationship.
The EAN (Effective Atomic Number) of central metal in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is:
Co(III): 27 electrons. 6 NH₃ donate 12 electrons. EAN = 27 + 12 = 39? Wait: Co(III) means 27-3=24 electrons + 6×2=12 = 36. EAN = 36 (Krypton). Sidgwick theory predicts stable complexes.
Mass of 1.5 moles of CO₂ (C=12, O=16):
K: violet (lilac). Na: golden yellow. Ca: brick red. Ba: apple green. Cu: blue-green. Colors due to electron transitions.
Inductive effect is permanent polarization of σ-bonds due to EN difference. Weakens with distance. Operates in saturated compounds.
The standard electrode potential of Zn²⁺/Zn is −0.76 V and Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34 V. The EMF of cell Zn|Zn²⁺||Cu²⁺|Cu is:
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V. Spontaneous reaction (positive EMF): Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.
For a zero-order reaction with k = 0.02 mol/L·s and initial concentration 1 M, time for completion:
For zero order: t = [A]₀/k = 1/0.02 = 50 s. Half-life = [A]₀/(2k) = 25 s.
Langmuir adsorption isotherm assumes monolayer adsorption. At high P, surface gets saturated (x/m approaches maximum).
Which is strongest acid among HClO, HClO₂, HClO₃, HClO₄?
Acid strength increases with oxidation state and number of oxygens (more O = more electron withdrawal from O-H bond). HClO₄ (perchloric acid) is one of strongest acids known.
Slag formed in extraction of copper from Cu₂S:
Copper extraction: CuFeS₂ (copper pyrite) → roasted. FeS oxidized: FeS + O₂ → FeO + SO₂. FeO + SiO₂ → FeSiO₃ (slag). Cu₂S reduced to Cu.
Inductive effect: polarization of σ bonds due to EN difference, weakens with distance. Resonance through π bonds, doesn't weaken with distance.
Longest chain: 3 carbons (propanal) with 2 methyl groups on C2: 2,2-dimethylpropanal. CHO has priority, gets C1.
R-NH₂ + CHCl₃ + KOH → R-NC (isocyanide, foul smell). Test for primary amines (aliphatic and aromatic). Forms toxic isocyanides.
The halogen that is liquid at room temperature:
Bromine (Br) is reddish-brown liquid at room temp. F, Cl are gases; I is solid (sublimes).
Acetone on reaction with NaOH and I₂ gives:
Iodoform test: methyl ketones (R-CO-CH₃) react with I₂/NaOH to give yellow CHI₃ (iodoform) + R-COO⁻. Positive test for CH₃CO- group.
Quantum numbers n=3, l=2 represent which orbital?
n=3 (3rd shell), l=2 (d orbital). So 3d orbital. Contains max 10 electrons.
Aniline is less basic than methylamine because:
Aniline is more soluble in water
Lone pair on N is delocalized into benzene ring
In aniline, N lone pair delocalizes into benzene ring (resonance), less available for protonation. Methylamine: +I effect of CH₃ increases electron density on N → more basic.
Buffer solution of NH₃ and NH₄Cl has pH around (Kb of NH₃ = 1.8×10⁻⁵):
pOH = pKb + log([salt]/[base]) = 4.74 + log(1) = 4.74 (when equal). pH = 14 − 4.74 = 9.26. Basic buffer.
Free radical polymerization at high pressure
LDPE: high pressure (1000-3000 atm), high T, peroxide initiator. Branched polymer, less dense. Used in plastic bags.
The crystal field splitting for octahedral complex depends on:
Crystal Field Theory: Δ depends on metal (oxidation state, geometry) and ligand (spectrochemical series). Strong field ligand → larger Δ → low spin.
For PCl₅ ⇌ PCl₃ + Cl₂, Kp = 2 at 500 K. At equilibrium with all gases at 1 atm each:
Qp = (p_PCl₃)(p_Cl₂)/p_PCl₅ = 1×1/1 = 1. Qp < Kp (1 < 2), so reaction proceeds forward.
Benzene has how many pi electrons?
Benzene: 6 C atoms in ring, each contributes 1 p electron. 6 π electrons total, delocalized. Aromatic (Hückel: 4n+2 = 6, n=1).
Quotient Q = 10, Kc = 100. Reaction will shift:
Q < K: reaction proceeds forward to reach equilibrium (more products form). Net reaction converts reactants to products.
Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because:
Phenoxide ion is stabilized by resonance
Phenoxide ion (C₆H₅O⁻) is stabilized by resonance; negative charge delocalized into ring. Ethoxide has no such stabilization. So phenol is more acidic (pKa ~10 vs 16).
The sugar present in milk is:
Lactose is milk sugar, disaccharide of glucose + galactose. Sucrose (cane sugar): glucose + fructose. Maltose: glucose + glucose.
Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ at 500 K, Kp/Kc equals:
Hf and Zr have nearly same size
Poor shielding by 4f electrons leads to contraction. Hf (5d) similar size to Zr (4d). Hard to separate, often found together in ores.
Adsorption forms new bonds (surface-adsorbate), releasing energy. Exothermic. Physisorption (weak) < chemisorption (strong) in ΔH.
ΔH for ice → water at 0°C is 6 kJ/mol. ΔS for this process is:
At equilibrium (melting point): ΔG = 0 → ΔS = ΔH/T = 6000/273 = 21.98 J/(K·mol). Phase change at constant T.
Brown ring test is used for detection of:
Add FeSO₄ to nitrate solution, then carefully add conc. H₂SO₄. Brown ring of [Fe(H₂O)₅NO]²⁺ at interface. Specific for NO₃⁻.
The dispersed phase in smoke is:
Smoke = solid particles (carbon) dispersed in gas (air). Aerosol. Fog is liquid droplets in gas.
Number of chiral carbons in glucose is:
Glucose (open chain): C2, C3, C4, C5 are chiral (each bonded to H, OH, and two different groups). Total 4 chiral centers → 2⁴ = 16 stereoisomers.
C₅H₁₂ isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane), neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane). 3 structural isomers.
Number of electrons in outermost shell of Cl (Z=17):
Cl: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵. Outermost (3rd shell): 2+5 = 7 electrons. Halogen, group 17. Forms Cl⁻ by gaining 1 e.
Δn_gas = moles products − moles reactants = 2 − (1+3) = −2. Kp = Kc(RT)^(−2). Reducing gas moles.
F = N_A × e = 6.022×10²³ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 96500 C/mol. Charge of 1 mole of electrons.
4 carbons → butanoic acid (butyric acid, found in rancid butter). Carboxyl C is C1.
POP = CaSO₄·½H₂O (calcium sulfate hemihydrate). Made by heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) at 120°C. Sets to gypsum when mixed with water.
Amino acid with no chiral carbon:
Glycine: H₂N-CH₂-COOH. R = H, so α-carbon has 2 H's (no chirality). Only achiral natural amino acid.
Opposite of carbocations! Carbanions: less alkyl substitution = more stable (less +I destabilization). Methyl most stable.
Order of reaction with rate = k[A]^(1/2)[B] is:
Order = sum of exponents in rate law = 1/2 + 1 = 3/2. Fractional orders indicate complex mechanism.
Common ion effect: addition of NH₄Cl to NH₃ solution:
NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻. Adding NH₄Cl (common ion NH₄⁺) shifts equilibrium left, reducing [OH⁻]. pH decreases.
Wurtz: 2RX + 2Na (dry ether) → R-R + 2NaX. Coupling of alkyl halides. Useful for symmetric alkanes. Dry ether essential.
Number of orbitals = 2l+1. For l=2: 5 orbitals (d_xy, d_yz, d_xz, d_x²-y², d_z²). Max 10 electrons.
The acidic oxide among the following is:
Non-metal oxides are acidic. CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ (acid). Metal oxides (Na₂O, CaO, MgO) are basic.
Average rate for reaction at 300 K with k = 0.05 /s and [A]₀ = 2 M:
For first-order: rate = k[A]. Initial rate = 0.05 × 2 = 0.1 M/s. Decreases as [A] decreases.
Period 2 element resembles Period 3 element of next group (lower-right diagonal). Li-Mg, Be-Al, B-Si are classic examples.
Given bond energies: H-H = 436, Cl-Cl = 242, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol. The ΔH for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl is:
ΔH = Σ BE(reactants broken) − Σ BE(products formed) = (436 + 242) − 2(431) = 678 − 862 = −184 kJ. Exothermic reaction.
Buna-S: butadiene + styrene copolymer. Synthetic rubber. S stands for styrene, Bu for butadiene, Na for sodium catalyst.
Oxidation of primary alcohol with mild oxidant gives:
Primary alcohol + mild oxidant (PCC, pyridinium chlorochromate) → aldehyde. With strong oxidant (KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺) → carboxylic acid.
Antacids neutralize stomach acid (HCl). NaHCO₃, Mg(OH)₂, Al(OH)₃ are common. Side effects: gas, diarrhea/constipation.
The secondary structure of protein is maintained by:
Secondary structure (α-helix, β-sheet) is stabilized by H-bonds between C=O and N-H of peptide backbone. Primary structure uses peptide bonds.
The rate of a reaction doubles when temperature increases from 300 K to 310 K. The activation energy is approximately:
Alkenes react with Br₂ in CCl₄ (decolorization test) via mechanism:
Br₂ adds across C=C via bromonium ion intermediate. Anti addition (trans product). Test for unsaturation.
Oxidation state of Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇:
K₂Cr₂O₇: 2(+1) + 2(Cr) + 7(−2) = 0 → 2Cr = 14 − 2 = 12 → Cr = +6. Powerful oxidizing agent in acidic medium.
Tollens' oxidizes aldehydes to carboxylic acids (silver mirror). Formaldehyde is most easily oxidized. Ketones don't react.
The electrophile in Friedel-Crafts acylation is:
RCOCl + AlCl₃ → RCO⁺ + AlCl₄⁻. Acylium ion attacks benzene to form aryl ketone. Less rearrangement than alkylation.
Which molecule has zero dipole moment?
CO₂ is linear (O=C=O), so individual C=O bond dipoles cancel. H₂O (bent), NH₃ (trigonal pyramidal), CHCl₃ (tetrahedral with polar bonds) all have net dipole.
A buffer solution contains 0.1 M CH₃COOH and 0.1 M CH₃COONa (Ka = 1.8×10⁻⁵). The pH is:
Henderson equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = −log(1.8×10⁻⁵) + log(1) = 4.74 + 0 = 4.74. Acetic acid buffer is classic.
Volume of 0.1 M NaOH needed to neutralize 25 mL of 0.2 M HCl:
Moles HCl = 0.025 × 0.2 = 0.005. Moles NaOH = same. V = 0.005/0.1 = 0.05 L = 50 mL. 1:1 stoichiometry.
Which compound has +7 oxidation state of Mn?
In KMnO₄: K(+1), O(−2 each, −8 total). Mn + 1 − 8 = −1 (charge on ion) → Mn = +7. Highest oxidation state for Mn.
A first order reaction is 25% complete in 30 min. Rate constant (k) is:
25% complete means 75% remaining. ln(C₀/C) = kt. ln(1/0.75) = 30k → 0.2877 = 30k → k = 0.00959 /min. Half-life = 0.693/k = 72 min.
Number of unpaired electrons in Cu²⁺ (d⁹):
Cu²⁺: [Ar] 3d⁹. One unpaired electron in d-shell. Paramagnetic. Blue color in aqueous solution due to d-d transitions.
N has 5 valence electrons. 3 bonds + 1 lone pair → sp³ hybridization, tetrahedral electronic, trigonal pyramidal molecular.
Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + ZnCl₂) reacts fastest with:
Lucas test: 3° alcohol reacts immediately (cloudiness), 2° takes 5-10 min, 1° requires heating. Carbocation stability drives SN1.
The product of Wurtz reaction: 2 CH₃Cl + 2Na in dry ether gives:
2 CH₃Cl + 2 Na → CH₃−CH₃ + 2 NaCl (dry ether). Two alkyl halides join to form longer alkane. Symmetric products from same halide.
Mass of Cu deposited by passing 0.5 A for 1 hour through CuSO₄ (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, atomic mass 63.5):
Buna-N: copolymer of butadiene and acrylonitrile. Oil-resistant synthetic rubber. Used in fuel hoses, gaskets.
Colloidal particles scatter light due to size comparable to wavelength of visible light, causing Tyndall effect. True solutions don't scatter.
Hybridization of Xe in XeF₄ is:
XeF₄: 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs = 6 hybrid orbitals → sp³d². Square planar geometry (lone pairs axial).
Dacron (PET): condensation of ethylene glycol (HO-CH₂-CH₂-OH) and terephthalic acid (benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid). Synthetic fiber.
Oxidation state of S in H₂SO₄:
H₂SO₄: H(+1)×2, O(−2)×4. Sum = 0. 2 + S − 8 = 0 → S = +6. Maximum oxidation state for S.
The osmotic pressure of 0.1 M glucose solution at 27°C is (R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K):
π = CRT = 0.1 × 0.0821 × 300 = 2.463 atm. Used to determine molar mass of macromolecules.
The oxidation number of Co in [CoCl(NH₃)₅]²⁺:
Complex charge = +2. NH₃ neutral, Cl = −1. x + (−1) + 0 = +2 → x = +3. Cobalt(III).
Most abundant allotrope of carbon in nature:
Graphite is thermodynamically more stable than diamond at room T/P. Diamond requires high pressure for stability.
Which cation gives white precipitate with NaOH, soluble in excess NaOH?
Al³⁺ + 3NaOH → Al(OH)₃ (white ppt) → Na[Al(OH)₄] (soluble). Amphoteric. Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Ba²⁺ hydroxides are not amphoteric.
6 bond pairs, no lone pair on S → octahedral. Bond angle 90°. Symmetric, non-polar.
F has highest EN = 4.0 (Pauling scale). Across a period, EN increases. Down a group, EN decreases. Order: F > O > Cl > N.
Number of molecules in 11.2 L of CO₂ at STP:
At STP, 22.4 L = 1 mol = 6.022×10²³ molecules. 11.2 L = 0.5 mol = 3.011×10²³ molecules.
Oxidation of tertiary alcohol with KMnO₄ gives:
Resistance to oxidation (no reaction under mild conditions)
3° alcohols have no α-H, resistant to oxidation. Strong oxidants can cleave C-C bonds (degradation).
In SN2 mechanism, inversion of configuration occurs. This is called:
Nucleophile attacks from back side (opposite leaving group) → inversion like umbrella turning inside out. Walden inversion. Complete inversion in SN2.
Number of unpaired electrons in Fe³⁺ (Z=26) is:
Fe³⁺: [Ar] 3d⁵. 5 unpaired electrons in d-orbitals (Hund's rule). More paramagnetic than Fe²⁺ (4 unpaired).
Ozone: bent structure due to lone pair. Expected 120° (sp²) but reduced to 116.8° due to lone pair repulsion.
AgBr decomposes to Ag + Br in light (blackens). Used in photographic film. Light exposure creates latent image, developed chemically.
Why do transition metals show variable oxidation states?
Vacant d orbitals and similar energies
ns and (n−1)d electrons have similar energies. Both can participate in bonding. Variable oxidation states from losing different numbers of d and s electrons.
BCl₃ is covalent (B and Cl are non-metals). B is electron deficient (6 electrons in outer shell) → strong Lewis acid.
Inert pair effect is most pronounced in:
Heavier p-block elements (6th period) show reluctance of ns² electrons to participate in bonding. Stable lower oxidation states: Tl⁺, Pb²⁺, Bi³⁺.
For a reaction with ΔH = −50 kJ and ΔS = −100 J/K at 300 K, the reaction is:
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = −50000 − 300×(−100) = −50000 + 30000 = −20000 J = −20 kJ. ΔG < 0 → spontaneous. Even though ΔS < 0, large negative ΔH dominates at low T.
Sucrose (cane sugar) = glucose + fructose. Hydrolyzed by sucrase (invertase). 'Invert sugar' due to optical rotation change.
SCE: Hg/Hg₂Cl₂/KCl(sat). E = +0.244 V vs SHE. Used as reference electrode; convenient, stable, non-toxic compared to SHE.
Which is the strongest reducing agent among Group 15 hydrides?
Reducing power increases down group: NH₃ < PH₃ < AsH₃ < SbH₃ < BiH₃. Larger atom = weaker bond with H = better reducing agent.
MO configuration of O₂ (12 valence electrons) gives bond order:
σ(2s)² σ*(2s)² σ(2p_z)² π(2p_x)² π(2p_y)² π*(2p_x)¹ π*(2p_y)¹. Bonding=8, Anti=4. BO=(8−4)/2=2. Paramagnetic (2 unpaired).
The volume of CO₂ liberated at STP when 50 g of CaCO₃ reacts with excess HCl is (Ca=40, C=12, O=16):
CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Moles CaCO₃ = 50/100 = 0.5 mol. So 0.5 mol CO₂ formed. Volume = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 L.
Most abundant element in Earth's crust (by mass):
Earth's crust (by mass): O (46.6%), Si (27.7%), Al (8.1%), Fe (5%), Ca (3.6%). Oxygen most abundant.
Hinsberg reagent is used to distinguish:
Benzenesulfonyl chloride (Hinsberg reagent): 1° amines give soluble product in KOH; 2° give insoluble; 3° don't react. Distinguishes amine classes.
Bakelite = phenol-formaldehyde resin. Condensation polymerization; cross-linked thermosetting plastic. Used in electrical switches, handles.
Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with CH₃Cl and AlCl₃ gives:
AlCl₃ generates CH₃⁺ (electrophile) from CH₃Cl. Benzene attacks CH₃⁺ → toluene. AlCl₃ regenerated. Used in dye and pharma industry.
For a first-order reaction, the half-life is 100 min. The rate constant is approximately:
For first order: t₁/₂ = 0.693/k → k = 0.693/100 = 6.93×10⁻³ min⁻¹. Independent of initial concentration.
Dehydration of ethanol with conc. H₂SO₄ at 170°C gives:
At 170°C: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (elimination, intra). At 140°C: 2C₂H₅OH → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O (substitution, inter).
Period 2: Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F, Ne. F has highest EN (4.0). Increases across period (left to right), decreases down group.
The wavelength of an electron moving with velocity 10⁶ m/s is (m = 9.1×10⁻³¹ kg, h = 6.6×10⁻³⁴ J·s):
10 g CaCO₃ (M=100) on strong heating gives CaO. Mass of CaO formed (M=56):
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Moles CaCO₃ = 0.1. Moles CaO = 0.1. Mass = 0.1 × 56 = 5.6 g. (Mass decreases as CO₂ escapes.)
Product of Cannizzaro reaction on benzaldehyde:
2 C₆H₅CHO + NaOH → C₆H₅CH₂OH + C₆H₅COONa. Cannizzaro (no α-H aldehydes): disproportionation.
Number of carbon atoms in glucose:
Glucose = C₆H₁₂O₆. Hexose (6-carbon sugar). Aldohexose: 6 C, aldehyde group. Most abundant monosaccharide in nature.
Silver nitrate gives white precipitate with chloride. Formula of precipitate:
Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl↓ (white, curdy). Soluble in NH₄OH. Photo-sensitive (darkens in light, used in photography).
For reaction A + B → products, doubling [A] doubles rate, doubling [B] has no effect. Rate law:
First order in A, zero in B. Overall first order. B doesn't appear in rate law; may be in fast equilibrium.
The coordination number of Pt in [PtCl₆]²⁻ is:
6 Cl⁻ ligands around Pt. Coordination number 6, octahedral geometry. Oxidation state of Pt = +4.
For first-order reaction, after 3 half-lives, the fraction remaining is:
After n half-lives: (1/2)ⁿ. For n=3: 1/8. Independent of initial concentration.
Number of sigma bonds in benzene:
Benzene C₆H₆: 6 C-C σ + 6 C-H σ = 12 σ bonds. Plus 3 π bonds (delocalized). Total 12 σ, 3 π.
Optical isomerism: non-superimposable mirror images. Usually requires chiral C (4 different groups). Rotation of plane-polarized light.
Energy of electron in first Bohr orbit of H is −13.6 eV. Energy in n=4:
E_n = −13.6/n² eV. E₄ = −13.6/16 = −0.85 eV. Approaches 0 (ionization) as n→∞.
2 moles of H₂ reacts with 1 mole O₂. Total moles of gas after reaction to form water vapor:
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O(g). 2 mol H₂ + 1 mol O₂ → 2 mol H₂O. Total gas moles: 2 (decreased by 1). Avogadro's law.
Magnetic moment of [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺ in BM (4 unpaired electrons):
μ = √(n(n+2)) BM where n = unpaired electrons. n=4: μ = √(4×6) = √24 = 4.90 BM. High-spin octahedral (H₂O is weak field).
Clemmensen: Zn(Hg)/HCl reduces C=O to CH₂. Clemmensen vs Wolff-Kishner (basic, N₂H₄/KOH) - same outcome different conditions.
Aniline on nitration with HNO₃/H₂SO₄ mainly gives:
In strongly acidic medium, -NH₂ is protonated to -NH₃⁺ (meta director). At low T with acetyl protection (-NHCOCH₃), gives ortho/para.
Resonance structure of carbonate ion has how many sigma and pi bonds?
CO₃²⁻ has 3 C-O σ bonds and 1 π bond delocalized over 3 oxygens (resonance). Each C-O bond has partial double bond character.
Most electronegative element in p-block is:
F has highest EN (4.0). p-block. Cl (3.16), O (3.44), N (3.04).
Which has lowest freezing point for 0.1 M aqueous solutions?
NaCl dissociates into 2 ions (i=2), others don't. More particles → greater ΔTf → lower FP.
Units of rate constant for second-order reaction:
For order n: [k] = (mol/L)^(1−n) · s⁻¹. For n=2: L·mol⁻¹·s⁻¹. For n=1: s⁻¹. For n=0: mol·L⁻¹·s⁻¹.
Baking powder = NaHCO₃ (sodium bicarbonate) + mild acid (tartaric/citric). Releases CO₂ on heating → makes baked goods rise.
Diazonium salt reacts with phenol in basic medium to give:
Diazonium + phenol → azo dye (orange-red). Coupling reaction (electrophilic aromatic substitution by diazonium ion).
Hardness of water is removed by which process at industrial scale?
Ion exchange resins replace Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ with Na⁺ (or H⁺). Permutit (Na-Al-silicate) is used. Regenerated with brine.
Styrene polymerizes to polystyrene. Hard, transparent plastic. Used in CD cases, insulation, disposable cups.
Which gas is responsible for greenhouse effect mainly?
CO₂ absorbs IR radiation emitted by Earth, trapping heat. Other greenhouse gases: CH₄, CFCs, N₂O, water vapor.
pH of 0.001 M H₂SO₄ (strong diprotic acid, both protons dissociate):
[H⁺] = 2 × 0.001 = 0.002 M. pH = −log(0.002) = 2.7. Each H₂SO₄ molecule gives 2 H⁺.
pH of 0.01 M NaOH solution is:
pOH = −log(10⁻²) = 2. pH = 14 − 2 = 12. Strong base fully dissociates.
For the exothermic reaction N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, the yield of NH₃ increases on:
Exothermic reaction favored by low T (Le Chatelier). 4 moles gas → 2 moles, so high P favors products. Used in Haber process: 200 atm, 450°C (compromise T for catalyst).
Time for 99% completion of first-order reaction with k = 0.01 /min:
For 99% complete: [A]/[A₀] = 0.01. ln(100) = kt. t = 4.605/0.01 = 460.5 min. (Half-life = 69 min; 99% needs ~6.6 half-lives.)
Element with highest melting point in d-block:
Tungsten has mp 3422°C, highest of all metals. Used in incandescent lamp filaments. Covalent bonding due to d-electrons.
The atomic radius of which is largest among Na, K, Rb, Cs?
Atomic radius increases down a group. Cs (bottom of group 1) has largest radius among alkali metals. Fr is below but radioactive.
The hybridization of carbon in CH₄ is:
CH₄: 4 σ bonds, no lone pair → sp³ hybridization. Tetrahedral geometry, 109.5° bond angles.
Cl has 7 valence electrons. With 3 F bonds + 2 lone pairs: 5 hybrid orbitals → sp³d. TBP electronic geometry, T-shape molecular (2 lone pairs equatorial).
Ni²⁺ (d⁸) with strong field ligand CN⁻ gives dsp² hybridization → square planar. With weak field ligands (Cl⁻), would be tetrahedral (sp³).
PVC: polyvinyl chloride. n CH₂=CHCl → (−CH₂−CHCl−)ₙ. Used in pipes, electrical insulation. Third-most produced plastic.
Given: C + O₂ → CO₂ ΔH = −393 kJ; C + ½O₂ → CO ΔH = −110 kJ. The ΔH for CO + ½O₂ → CO₂ is:
By Hess law: target = first − second. ΔH = −393 − (−110) = −283 kJ. Combustion of CO is highly exothermic.
Effect of temperature on physical adsorption:
Physisorption is exothermic. By Le Chatelier, increasing T shifts equilibrium backward (desorption). Decreases with T.
Ni²⁺ (d⁸) + strong field CN⁻: dsp² hybridization → square planar (low spin, diamagnetic). With weak field ligands (Cl⁻): tetrahedral (sp³).
Element with highest second ionization energy in 3rd period:
After 1st IE, Na loses its only valence electron. 2nd IE removes from inner complete octet → very high. Na⁺ has stable Ne config.
Anomalous behavior of Li is due to:
Li shows diagonal relationship with Mg. Small size → high charge density → strong polarizing power → covalent character in compounds.
Which is the strongest reducing agent among hydrogen halides?
Reducing power increases down the group as H-X bond strength decreases. HI has weakest H-I bond, easily gives H⁺ and I⁻ (good reducing agent).
Aniline reacts with bromine water to give:
Aniline (highly activated ring due to -NH₂) + Br₂ water → 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (white ppt) instantly. No catalyst needed.
Reaction of acetic acid with PCl₅:
RCOOH + PCl₅ → RCOCl + POCl₃ + HCl. OH replaced by Cl. Acid chloride is reactive acylating agent.
Tollens' [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺: oxidizes aldehydes (CHO → COOH). Ag⁺ reduced to Ag (mirror). Ketones don't react (no α-H needed).
Nernst equation at 25°C: E = E° − (0.0591/n) log Q. For Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, n is:
Balanced half-reactions: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻, Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. n = 2 electrons transferred.
Which is most common oxidation state of Mn?
+2 is most stable (d⁵ config). +7 (MnO₄⁻) is powerful oxidant. Both arise due to half-filled or fully-utilized d-shell stability.
Salicylic acid + acetic anhydride → aspirin + acetic acid. Acetylation of phenolic OH; analgesic and antipyretic.
2-butene (CH₃-CH=CH-CH₃) has different groups on each carbon of C=C, so cis and trans isomers exist. 1-butene and propene have CH₂=, no isomerism.
Lanthanides: La (57) to Lu (71). 15 elements (4f¹ to 4f¹⁴). Actinides: Ac (89) to Lr (103). f-block.
The gas liberated when dilute HCl reacts with FeS is:
FeS + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂S↑. H₂S has rotten egg smell, turns lead acetate paper black (PbS).
SHE defined as 0 V reference for all electrode potentials. [H⁺] = 1 M, P(H₂) = 1 atm, T = 298 K.
Natural rubber is a polymer of:
Natural rubber = cis-1,4-polyisoprene. Synthetic rubber (Neoprene) is polymer of chloroprene. Vulcanization with S improves properties.
The number of unpaired electrons in Fe²⁺ (Z=26) is:
Fe: [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². Fe²⁺: [Ar] 3d⁶. 3d subshell: ↑↓ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑ → 4 unpaired electrons. Fe²⁺ is paramagnetic.
Tertiary alkyl halide in polar solvent
SN1 proceeds via carbocation intermediate; 3° carbocation most stable. Polar protic solvent stabilizes ions. Rate = k[RX] only.
Molality of solution containing 36 g glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆, M=180) in 250 g water:

Number of peptide bonds in tripeptide:
Tripeptide = 3 amino acids joined by 2 peptide bonds. N-peptide has (N−1) peptide bonds.
Heavy water = D₂O (deuterium oxide). Used as moderator in nuclear reactors (slows neutrons). mp 3.8°C, bp 101.4°C.
Mixed acid generates NO₂⁺ (nitronium ion, electrophile). H₂SO₄ acts as acid catalyst. Benzene + NO₂⁺ → nitrobenzene.
Specific rate constant k for first-order reaction at 300 K is 0.05 /min. After 20 min, fraction remaining:
First order: [A] = [A₀]e^(−kt) = e^(−0.05×20) = e⁻¹ = 0.368. So 36.8% remaining after 20 min.
The IUPAC name of K₃[Fe(CN)₆] is:
K₃[Fe(CN)₆]: 3 K⁺ outside, complex has charge −3. 6 CN⁻ give −6, so Fe = +3. Hexacyanoferrate(III). Commonly called potassium ferricyanide.
Phenol can be distinguished from ethanol by:
Phenol + Br₂ water → 2,4,6-tribromophenol (white ppt). Ethanol doesn't react. Also, phenol gives violet color with FeCl₃.
Soap/detergent molecules in water above CMC
Soap molecules have hydrophilic head + hydrophobic tail. Above CMC (critical micelle concentration), they aggregate to form micelles.
Vitamin C is also known as:
Vitamin C = ascorbic acid, water-soluble. Deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums). Not synthesized by humans; needs dietary intake.
P has 5 valence electrons. 5 bond pairs → 5 hybrid orbitals → sp³d. Trigonal bipyramidal geometry.
The solubility product Ksp of AgCl is 1.6×10⁻¹⁰. The solubility of AgCl in water is:
AgCl ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻. Ksp = s² → s = √(Ksp) = √(1.6×10⁻¹⁰) = 1.26×10⁻⁵ M. Very low solubility.
The catalyst used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils is:
Finely divided nickel catalyzes hydrogenation of unsaturated oils to saturated fats. Vegetable oil + H₂ --Ni--> vegetable fat.
At 25°C, Kw = 10⁻¹⁴. In neutral solution, [H⁺] equals:
Hinsberg test: 2° amine gives product that is:
2° amines give sulfonyl derivative that is INSOLUBLE in KOH. 1° gives soluble (acidic H). 3° doesn't react. Distinguishing test.
Empirical = simplest whole number ratio. C:H:O = 6:12:6 = 1:2:1. So CH₂O. Molecular formula = (CH₂O)₆.
Photochemical smog: NOₓ + hydrocarbons + sunlight → O₃, PAN, aldehydes. Causes eye irritation. Classic smog (London) is reducing (SO₂).
Anomalous behavior of nitrogen due to:
Absence of d orbitals, small size
N can't expand octet (no d orbitals). Forms pπ-pπ multiple bonds (N₂, NO). Cannot form NF₅ (unlike P in PF₅).
The hardness of water is due to presence of:
Hardness is due to Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions. Temporary hardness (bicarbonates) removed by boiling; permanent hardness (sulfates/chlorides) requires ion exchange.
The pH of a 0.001 M HCl solution is:
HCl is strong acid: [H⁺] = 10⁻³ M. pH = −log(10⁻³) = 3. Pure water has pH 7; lower means acidic.
Slag formed in extraction of iron in blast furnace is:
Limestone (CaCO₃) decomposes to CaO, which combines with silica (SiO₂) impurity: CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (slag). Floats on molten iron.
The boiling point of 1 m aqueous solution of urea (Kb = 0.52 K·kg/mol) is:
ΔTb = Kb × m = 0.52 × 1 = 0.52°C. Boiling point = 100 + 0.52 = 100.52°C. Urea is non-electrolyte, so van't Hoff factor i = 1.
The oxidation state of nitrogen in HNO₃ is:
HNO₃: H(+1), O(−2 each, total −6). Sum = 0. N + 1 − 6 = 0 → N = +5. Maximum oxidation state for N.
Number of amino acids essential for humans:
9 essential amino acids (must come from diet): His, Ile, Leu, Lys, Met, Phe, Thr, Trp, Val. Body cannot synthesize.
2-butanol (CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃) has chiral C (4 different groups). 1-butanol, propanol, methanol have no chiral center.
Crystal field splitting for octahedral complex: d-orbitals split into:
In Oh field: d_xy, d_yz, d_xz (t₂g) between axes (lower E); d_x²-y², d_z² (e_g) along axes (higher E, repel ligands).
The vitamin responsible for blood clotting:
Vitamin K (Koagulation). Deficiency causes excessive bleeding. Fat-soluble; found in green leafy vegetables, synthesized by gut bacteria.
Standard reduction potential of Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34 V. Standard oxidation potential of Zn/Zn²⁺ is:
Standard oxidation potential = −(standard reduction potential). Zn²⁺/Zn has E°_red = −0.76 V, so Zn/Zn²⁺ has E°_ox = +0.76 V.
The most acidic oxide among the following is:
Acidic strength increases with oxidation state and EN of central atom. Cl₂O₇ (Cl in +7) is most acidic oxide. Order: Cl₂O₇ > SO₃ > P₄O₁₀ > N₂O₅.
The hybridization of carbon in C₂H₂ (acetylene) is:
C₂H₂: H-C≡C-H. Each C has 2 σ bonds (1 to H, 1 to other C) and 2 π bonds (triple bond). 2 σ → sp hybridization. Linear geometry, 180°.
VSEPR theory predicts the shape of molecule based on:
VSEPR: valence shell electron pair repulsion. Lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair repulsion.
10 g of H₂ reacts with 80 g of O₂ to form water. The limiting reagent is (H=1, O=16):
Moles H₂ = 10/2 = 5 mol. Moles O₂ = 80/32 = 2.5 mol. Reaction: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Required O₂ for 5 mol H₂ = 2.5 mol. Exactly available! Both fully consumed (stoichiometric).
μ = √(n(n+2)) BM. n=1: √3 = 1.73 BM. Low-spin octahedral (CN⁻ is strong field ligand).
The bond order of O₂ molecule is:
O₂: 12 valence electrons. MO config gives 8 bonding and 4 antibonding electrons. BO = (8−4)/2 = 2. Paramagnetic due to 2 unpaired electrons in π* orbitals.
Aldol condensation: carbonyl with α-H undergoes self-addition in base. Forms β-hydroxy aldehyde/ketone, dehydrates to α,β-unsaturated.
How many coulombs are required to deposit 1 mole of Al from molten Al₂O₃ (Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al)?
3 Faradays per mole of Al. Q = 3 × 96500 = 289500 C = 2.895×10⁵ C. Faraday's law: m = ZQ where Z = M/(nF).
The element with atomic number 21 belongs to which block?
Z=21 is Scandium (Sc). Electronic config: [Ar] 3d¹ 4s². Last electron enters d-subshell, so d-block (first transition element).
Strongest acid among CH₃COOH, FCH₂COOH, ClCH₂COOH, NC-CH₂COOH:
Acidity enhanced by -I (electron withdrawing) groups stabilizing conjugate base. Order: NC > F > Cl > CH₃. Stronger -I = stronger acid.
Saponification is reaction between fat and:
Saponification: ester (fat) + base (NaOH) → soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) + glycerol. Used in soap making.
Standard EMF of cell with E°_Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V and E°_Cu²+/Cu = +0.34 V:
Ag+ is stronger oxidizer (higher E°). Cell: Cu|Cu²⁺||Ag+|Ag. E° = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 − 0.34 = 0.46 V.
Anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr to propene requires:
In presence of peroxides (ROOR), HBr adds anti-Markovnikov (Kharasch effect). Free radical mechanism gives 1-bromopropane. Only works with HBr, not HCl or HI.
Both C₆H₁₂O₆. Glucose is aldose (CHO group), fructose is ketose (C=O group). Same molecular formula, different functional groups → functional isomers.
EDTA forms complex with Ca²⁺ with coordination number:
EDTA is hexadentate (2 N + 4 O donors). Forms octahedral complex with most metal ions including Ca²⁺. Used in titrations (water hardness).
Which compound exhibits strongest hydrogen bonding?
H-F has highest polarity among hydrogen halides (largest EN difference). Strongest H-bonding gives HF anomalously high boiling point (19.5°C) compared to HCl (−85°C).
Van't Hoff factor for AlCl₃ (assuming complete dissociation):
AlCl₃ → Al³⁺ + 3Cl⁻. Total 4 ions. i = 4. Colligative properties enhanced by factor i.
Bond angle in CH₄ is approximately:
sp³ hybridization, tetrahedral geometry, bond angle 109.5°. Maximizes separation of bond pairs.
The bond order of N₂ molecule is:
N₂ has 14 electrons. MO: σ(1s)² σ*(1s)² σ(2s)² σ*(2s)² π(2p)⁴ σ(2p)². Bonding=10, Antibonding=4. BO = (10−4)/2 = 3. Triple bond.
For the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, K_c = 4 at 500 K. If concentrations are [N₂]=1, [H₂]=1, [NH₃]=2 M, the reaction will:
Q_c = [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³) = 4/(1×1) = 4 = K_c. So reaction is at equilibrium. No net change in concentrations.
Reaction between carboxylic acid and alcohol (conc. H₂SO₄) gives:
Fischer esterification: RCOOH + R'OH → RCOOR' + H₂O (acid catalyst, reversible). Used in flavor/fragrance industry.
Ksp of AgBr is 5×10⁻¹³. Solubility in 0.1 M AgNO₃ solution is:
Ksp = [Ag⁺][Br⁻]. With 0.1 M Ag⁺ from AgNO₃: [Br⁻] = Ksp/[Ag⁺] = 5×10⁻¹³/0.1 = 5×10⁻¹² M. Common ion effect reduces solubility.
The van't Hoff factor for K₄[Fe(CN)₆] assuming complete dissociation is:
K₄[Fe(CN)₆] → 4K⁺ + [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ → 5 ions total. i = 5. Van't Hoff factor = (moles after dissociation)/(moles before).
The number of electrons in an atom of element with atomic number 26 (Fe) present in d-subshell is:
Fe: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 3d⁶. So d-subshell has 6 electrons. It's a d-block element, transition metal with variable oxidation states.
Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period. Cs (bottom of group 1, leftmost) has highest.
Maximum covalent character is shown by:
Fajans rules: smaller cation and larger anion = more covalent. Al³⁺ is small with high charge → maximum polarizing power → most covalent.
EAN rule predicts stability based on:
Effective atomic number equals noble gas
EAN = Z − oxidation_state + 2×coordination_number. For [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: 27 − 3 + 12 = 36 (Krypton). Sidgwick's rule.
The number of disulfide bridges in insulin is:
Insulin has 2 polypeptide chains (A and B) connected by 2 disulfide bridges, plus 1 internal disulfide in chain A. Total 3.
Benzene undergoes which type of reactions predominantly?
Benzene's aromatic stability favors substitution over addition (preserves aromaticity). Halogenation, nitration, sulfonation, Friedel-Crafts are typical EAS reactions.
Nylon-6: ring-opening polymerization of caprolactam. Used in textiles, gears. Nylon-6,6 is condensation of two monomers.
The molarity of a solution containing 5.85 g NaCl in 500 mL solution is (Na=23, Cl=35.5):
Moles NaCl = 5.85/58.5 = 0.1 mol. Molarity = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 M. Molarity = moles/volume(L).
Reaction of acetaldehyde with NaOH gives (aldol condensation):
2 CH₃CHO → CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO (3-hydroxybutanal, 'aldol'). α-H of one aldehyde attacks carbonyl of another. Heating dehydrates to α,β-unsaturated aldehyde.
The number of geometrical isomers of [Ma₂b₂] square planar complex is:
Square planar [Ma₂b₂]: cis (a's adjacent) and trans (a's opposite). 2 isomers. Tetrahedral would have only 1 (no isomers).
NH₃: sp³ with 1 lone pair. Ideal 109.5° reduced to 107° due to lone pair-bond pair repulsion (lone pair occupies more space).
RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O. Removes carbonyl carbon; gives primary amine with one less C.
Transition metal compounds are colored due to:
d-d transitions between split d-orbitals absorb visible light. Color = complement of absorbed. Example: Cu²⁺ absorbs red, appears blue.
